messages:
maya: Quick sync — I'm about to roll an ingest change for the embeddings endpoint. TL;DR: coerce non-string inputs (numbers/objects) to strings instead of rejecting. Two asks: compatibility check + deprecation plan for a future strict_mode that will opt-in to 400s.

sam: Heads-up — current behavior silently coerces numbers to strings in the client library, but server-side API has historically accepted only strings. New change makes server explicit about coercion and adds per-item metadata when coercion/truncation occurs. Default stays permissive (no breaking change).

li: Truncation details: we truncate by token budget using the model's tokenizer (model catalog tokenizers). We reserve ~32 tokens for prefix/system context. If an item exceeds model.max_input_tokens - 32 we cut at the last whole token. When that happens we return a per-item flag: "truncated": "true" and a short reason. We do NOT silently drop items or reorder.

anita: On empty/null inputs: plan is to treat null as an explicit empty string but mark it in response metadata ("null_item": "true"). That keeps indices stable for downstream consumers. We'll emit a zero-filled vector for nulls rather than omitting entries.

maya: Quick example request I'm planning to use in the rollout checklist: 

```json
POST /api/v1/embeddings
{
  "model": "redwood-embed-v2",
  "inputs": ["hello", 123, null, {"text": "hi"}],
  "strict_mode": false
}
```

sam: Example response shape we'll guarantee (note: vectors trimmed for brevity): 

```json
{
  "model": "redwood-embed-v2",
  "data": [
    {"input_index":0, "embedding": [0.012, -0.34, ...]},
    {"input_index":1, "embedding": [0.01, -0.31, ...], "coerced_from": "number"},
    {"input_index":2, "embedding": [0.0, 0.0, ...], "null_item": true},
    {"input_index":3, "embedding": [0.02, -0.10, ...], "coerced_from": "object"}
  ],
  "warnings": ["1 item coerced: index 1", "1 item coerced: index 3"]
}
```

li: On batch limits: operational limits are token-budget first (we cap request total tokens to protect runtime), but we also keep a soft cap of 4096 items per request for metadata sanity. The token cap is what will drive 413/503 fallback if exceeded. We'll document both.

anita: Back-compat and deprecation plan: we keep permissive mode as default for 90 days after rollout, then flip a telemetry-gated warning header ("X-Embed-Strict-Deprecation") to signal clients. After 120 more days we may enable strict_mode by default for a minor release with opt-in flags for enterprise. We'll announce well in changelog.

maya: One implementation Q: do we stringify objects as compact JSON or pick "text" field if present?

sam: Implementation will prefer "text" field if present and it's a string. Otherwise we fallback to JSON.stringify(obj). Reason: common SDKs send {text: ...}. We'll include an explicit example in the spec.

li: Also adding a per-item "metadata" map in the response for tracing tooling (e.g., {"truncated":true, "coerced_from":"object"}). That will help downstream debug without parsing vectors.

maya: Sounds good. Final checklist before canary: add unit tests for 1) number coercion, 2) object-with-text, 3) object-without-text, 4) null -> zero-vector, 5) truncation token boundary. I'll ping for CR review once tests exist.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout initiated: embedding-coerce-v1 -> eng-platform-canary-01 at 1766504400.

anita: Thanks — I'll update the compatibility doc and add the deprecation timeline. :thumbsup:

sam: Ping @maya when CR is up, I'll do review + perf check (token accounting). :ok_hand:

maya: Will do. Thanks everyone.
